title: Deep Reorganization: Retaining Residuals in TinyML
problem: Residual connections in deep neural networks require significant additional memory, making deployment on memory-constrained tiny devices difficult. Existing approaches eliminate residuals to reduce peak memory but suffer substantial accuracy degradation.
motivation: Enabling efficient deployment of accurate residual neural networks on memory-limited embedded devices without performance loss.
method: DERO rearranges how residual connections (shortcuts that add input values back to outputs in neural networks) execute while a model is running. It analyzes which operations happen inside each residual and how they depend on each other, then reorganizes the timing and storage location of data processing. This shrinks the peak memory needed at any one moment—matching the memory footprint of networks without residuals. The accuracy benefits of residuals are preserved because the final computation stays identical; only the storage order changes.
key_novelty: By rearranging when and where data is stored in residual connections based on analyzing their operations, you achieve the memory efficiency of networks without residuals while preserving the accuracy benefits that residuals provide.
contributions: Reorganization strategy for residual connections that reduces peak memory without eliminating residuals
Achieves peak memory comparable to non-residual baseline models while maintaining original accuracy
Evaluation across diverse computer vision model architectures demonstrating generalizability
Practical solution for deploying residual networks on resource-constrained embedded devices

metrics.other: peak memory usage comparable to non-residual models

primary_theme: Memory-efficient residual connections for embedded inference
